name: plate-47-satellite-labels
version_tag: #145 SATELLITE LABELS — month names on the month wheel, 1-12 on feb and leap. TWO COLOUR, same AMS mapping as plate-45: slot 1 BLACK, slot 2 WHITE. Supersedes 141/142/143 (printed, unlabelled) — the mesh is bit-identical, only the top faces are engraved. WHICH TOOTH IS WHICH MONTH was measured from the simulator's calendar engine, not assumed: at 23:00 on date 30 the 23h arm sweeps the wheel and whichever tooth is on the strike line IS that month's tooth, true for all twelve and single-valued over 14 simulated years. The five strike teeth come out JUN NOV APR SEP FEB going round from the strike line — February plus the four 30-day months, which is the check Ron can make by eye on the printed part. An algebraic shortcut (+7 teeth/month) got this WRONG; the tooth index runs against the spin so the step is -7, and the engine caught it. ENGRAVING THE STRIKE TEETH IS DEFENDED, not assumed safe: the bars take the 24h arm's push, and a 2.6 x 0.5mm groove drops their section modulus to 57% of solid — but it sits at r10.85 where the bending moment is 37% of the root's, so peak stress there is 58% of the root's and the critical section stays at the root. Moving the label inboard would have inverted that. GLYPHS: '4' and 'A' are drawn OPEN. Their counters are inherently tiny in a stroke font and fill in at any printable stroke and any cap that still fits between hub r4.00 and mesh root r13.87 — the first cut printed 4, 6, 8, 9, 0 as blobs. Scaling does not rescue them; the letterform had to change. All counters now clear 0.25mm2. Kern 0.75 > stroke 0.45, or adjacent letters fuse (the first cut read as 18 blobs instead of 36 letters). REGISTRATION: each ink body carries its own offset from its receiver because compose centres every object on its own bbox and they differ. Do not tidy them. ALSO CARRIES THE #146 ARM REPRINT: 145_carrier_feb and 146_carrier_leap ride along in BLACK (extruder 1, no ink). The arms that came off plate-44 rev D are scrap — their pivot pad overhung the press-fit bore by 1.29mm across 120 deg of its rim, so the lip printed unsupported over the hole and would foul a slightly-long post at assembly. They are two small parts and there was bed to spare, so they do not need a plate of their own. 8 objects (3 receivers + 3 ink + 2 arms), flat, no supports, xy-comp -0.06. | QUIET.
